minutes.headline: Water commissioners hold that a 40B development outside the district gets no water; counsel to advise on the response.
minutes.summary: The board briefly discussed a stalled hiring search, then spent most of the meeting on a 40B application for a Howard Street development that it considers outside the district. It agreed to send the application and public comments to its attorney, who is to help draft the board's response letter. It also discussed equipment replacement and a bond for a new building, then adjourned.

public_comment.topic: A resident asked about tank elevation versus the proposed site and whether private water companies are supplied.
Mr. Rogers urged the board to keep to the point that the site is outside the district, rely on counsel, and have counsel draft the response.
A speaker urged gathering wider resident support, such as by postcard or email, against expanding the district.

budget_items.what_was_said: The one remaining candidate's salary expectation may be well above what the district can offer; the previous employee's pay was suggested as a guide.

budget_items.topic: Offsite utilities cost in the 40B application
budget_items.what_was_said: The application's offsite utilities budget for water and sewer was called inaccurate, though members said the developer would bear the cost.
A member recalled an earlier estimate of monthly upkeep for a booster pump site.

budget_items.topic: Projected water revenue from the development
budget_items.what_was_said: A member roughly estimated annual water revenue from the proposed units as small.
A storage tank for the development was estimated in a range.
Members discussed replacing aging equipment and a backhoe, with differing cost estimates, and asked for prices and a capital plan.
The district reported strong revenue because of high water use during the pandemic.
The bond went out to bid and a rate was mentioned; a term of about 30 years was discussed and paperwork is to be signed next week.

decisions.decision: Send the 40B application, articles of organization and public considerations to the board's attorney for a view on the district's position.
Hold a special meeting next Wednesday at four o'clock to sign bond paperwork, with the 40B matter added as a running agenda item.
Superintendent to put together equipment needs and prices for the board to consider as a capital plan.

what_happened.line: The Water District board spent most of the meeting on a 40B application for a Howard Street development, which it considers to be outside the district.
The board agreed to send the application, articles of organization and public considerations to its attorney for a view on the district's position.
A special meeting is set for next Wednesday at four o'clock to sign bond paperwork, with the 40B matter added as a running agenda item.
The superintendent is to put together equipment needs and prices for the board to consider as a capital plan.
The board put a hiring search on hold to seek other applicants, citing a salary expectation that may be above what the district can offer.

why_it_matters: Whether a 40B development outside the district can draw on district water bears on who pays for new supply infrastructure, and on whether the district's service area grows.
The bond for a new building and the planned equipment purchases are district capital costs, which can reach water rates and user bills.
